economy.summary: His campaign site says his focus is helping local businesses create jobs in the county and reducing government over-regulation.
economy.short: Focuses on local job creation and reducing government over-regulation.

taxes.summary: Responding to the governor's $53.26 billion 2026-27 budget proposal, said he is uncomfortable with the amount of spending, opposed transferring $4.58 billion from the Rainy Day Fund to cover expenses, and opposed the proposed new taxes on skill games and marijuana.
taxes.short: Opposes proposed spending level, Rainy Day Fund transfer, new taxes.

abortion.summary: Voted against House Bill 1957, a proposed amendment to the Pennsylvania Constitution providing for personal reproductive liberty, which passed the House 102-101 in December 2025. His campaign site also lists him as pro-life.
abortion.short: Voted against reproductive-liberty constitutional amendment; campaign lists pro-life.

education.summary: In a 2019 interview he said he supports the Educational Improvement Tax Credit, which lets businesses direct tax dollars toward scholarship and educational organizations, and called the hold-harmless school funding policy critical for western Pennsylvania districts with declining enrollment.
education.short: Supports Educational Improvement Tax Credit and hold-harmless school funding.

energy.summary: His legislative site says he supports responsibly harvesting Pennsylvania's abundant natural resources in a way that promotes economic growth while protecting the state's environmental integrity.
energy.short: Supports developing natural resources while protecting environmental integrity.

guns.summary: Voted against House Bill 1593, a bill to extend background-check requirements to private firearm sales, which passed the House 104-99 in September 2025. His campaign site also lists him as pro-Second Amendment.
guns.short: Voted against extending background checks to private firearm sales.
